$description:
Named text styles. VISUAL sizes, deliberately decoupled from HTML heading levels — an <h2> can carry headline-hero and an <h1> can carry headline-tiny. Use heading tags for document structure, these classes for appearance.

size and weight reference variables; leading and tracking are literal. Weight is a real scale tied to the typeface and changes per client. Leading and tracking are functions of size — that two headlines share a leading value is not shared meaning, it is both of them being large. Naming them as a scale would imply you might change one independently of size, and you would not.

Air Methods (AIRMETHODS-SC-TOKEN-SPEC §7, T2/T5/T6): display headlines Hero–Medium are the condensed family at Black, uppercase; Small/Tiny are the subhead tier — Text family at ExtraBold, because Air Methods' subheads are body-family-800, not condensed. Body leading 1.65 is theirs, measured. `case` is optional and emits text-transform.

$headingDefaults.$description: Fallback for BARE heading tags — what a CMS produces with no class. Utilities sit in a later layer, so an explicit .text-style-* always wins.
